knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says to confirm the check-in system before starting and not to rely on a single unreliable channel. A friend's text is not an approved escalation.
The lesson says not to confront an aggressive person or investigate a suspected crime, and to use the escalation tree or emergency services in immediate danger.
The control access and personal safety section says not to confront an aggressive person or attempt to investigate a suspected crime.

practicalCriteria: Learner completes procedure step 1: Establish whether the task is lone work, and review the organisation's lone-work policy and the site-specific risk assessment.
Learner completes procedure step 2: Confirm the supervisor contact, the start and finish times, the check-in intervals and the communication device before starting.
Learner completes procedure step 3: Confirm the missed check-in escalation procedure, and do not rely on a single communication channel.
Learner completes procedure step 4: On arrival, check authorised entry, lighting, exits and safe parking.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 8: Record check-in outcomes and concerns without collecting unnecessary location history, then debrief and update the risk assessment.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 3 is not done: Confirm the missed check-in escalation procedure, and do not rely on a single communication channel.
Stop work if procedure step 5 is not done: Avoid any area where occupants, animals, threats or hazardous conditions create unmanaged risk, and do not confront an aggressive person.
Stop work if procedure step 6 is not done: Make each agreed check-in on time, and if contact is missed, follow the escalation procedure and notify the supervisor.
